title: F172 - Lesson 12: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing & Research Workshop
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing & Research Workshop: Molecular Engine, NHEJ vs HDR, Casgevy Case Study, and NEA Task 2 Distinction Checklist
deliverable: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology (Unit F172: Genetics) Lesson 12 presentation covering bacterial CRISPR immunity origins, sgRNA and PAM 5'-NGG-3' targeting, Cas9 endonuclease cleavage, cellular repair pathways (NHEJ knockout vs HDR template correction), clinical milestone Casgevy (ex-vivo BCL11A editing for sickle cell disease), and an advanced evaluative workshop for NEA Task 2.

objectives.knowledge: Explain the molecular anatomy and action of the CRISPR-Cas9 endonuclease system (crRNA/tracrRNA sgRNA, PAM motif, RuvC/HNH catalytic domains).
objectives.application: Compare DNA repair mechanisms: error-prone Non-Homologous End Joining (NHEJ) knockout vs precision Homology-Directed Repair (HDR) knock-in.
objectives.evaluation: Critique clinical applications (Casgevy BCL11A silencing) against ANT-130 RNAi and apply Distinction criteria to coursework evaluations.

terminology.def: Adaptive bacterial immune system repurposed as a precision gene-editing tool; uses a single guide RNA (sgRNA) to direct Cas9 endonuclease to cut target DNA.
A short 5'-NGG-3' DNA sequence immediately adjacent to the target site, required for Cas9 binding and strand unwinding.
An error-prone repair pathway directly re-ligating double-strand breaks, frequently creating indels that knockout gene function.
A high-fidelity repair pathway using an exogenous DNA donor template to introduce precise sequence corrections or insertions.
The first approved CRISPR therapy; edits patient HSPCs via NHEJ to disrupt the BCL11A erythroid enhancer, reactivating fetal hemoglobin (HbF) in sickle cell disease.

slides.title: F172 Lesson 12: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing & Research Workshop
slides.subtitle: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology · Unit F172: Genetics (Dan)
keyTakeaways: Molecular engine of CRISPR-Cas9, repair pathways, and clinical therapies.
Dedicated NEA Task 2 Distinction evaluative research workshop.

slides.title: Biological Origins: Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
slides.subtitle: CRISPR loci, viral memory spacers, and targeted cleavage of bacteriophages
keyTakeaways: CRISPR loci store captured fragments of invading bacteriophage DNA as spacers.
Transcribed crRNA and tracrRNA guide Cas endonucleases to recognize re-invading phage genomes.
Cleaves viral DNA upon re-infection, providing adaptive prokaryotic immune defense.

slides.title: The CRISPR-Cas9 Engine: 3 Essential Components
slides.subtitle: Single guide RNA (sgRNA), PAM motif (5'-NGG-3'), and Cas9 endonuclease
keyTakeaways: sgRNA: 20-nucleotide synthetic spacer matching genomic target fused to tracrRNA scaffold.
PAM Motif: 5'-NGG-3' sequence essential for initial Cas9 binding and DNA strand separation.
Cas9 Endonuclease: Catalytic RuvC and HNH domains induce targeted blunt double-strand breaks.

slides.title: Step-by-Step Mechanism of Cas9 Target Cleavage
slides.subtitle: PAM interrogation, DNA unwinding, R-loop formation, and double-strand break
keyTakeaways: 1. PAM Interrogation: Cas9 scans genomic DNA for 5'-NGG-3' motifs.
2. DNA Unwinding: Cas9 unwinds adjacent duplex, testing sgRNA complementarity.
3. R-Loop Formation: Stable 20 bp RNA:DNA hybrid locks endonuclease in place.
4. Double-Strand Break: RuvC and HNH domains cut both DNA strands 3 bp upstream of PAM.

slides.title: DNA Repair Pathway 1: NHEJ Gene Knockout
slides.subtitle: Error-prone re-ligation, indel creation, and targeted gene disruption
keyTakeaways: Non-Homologous End Joining directly re-ligates broken ends without a repair template.
Frequently inserts or deletes nucleotides (indels), creating reading frame-shifts.
Ideal for knocking out pathogenic dominant genes, viral entry receptors, or silencer enhancers.

slides.title: DNA Repair Pathway 2: HDR Gene Correction
slides.subtitle: High-fidelity template-directed repair for precise base correction
keyTakeaways: Homology-Directed Repair utilizes an exogenous synthetic donor DNA repair template.
Enables exact nucleotide substitution, point mutation repair, or sequence knock-in.
Active primarily in S/G2 phases of dividing cells; inefficient in non-dividing adult neurons.

slides.title: Clinical Landmark: Casgevy for Sickle Cell Disease
slides.subtitle: First regulatory-approved CRISPR-Cas9 ex vivo therapy (Vertex / CRISPR Therapeutics)
keyTakeaways: Ex vivo editing of autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs).
NHEJ disrupts the GATA1-binding site in the erythroid enhancer of BCL11A.
Reactivates fetal hemoglobin (HbF, α2γ2), preventing sickle polymerization and pain crises.

slides.title: Technical Obstacles: Off-Target Cleavage & Delivery
slides.subtitle: Mismatch tolerance, p53 activation, and in vivo vector packaging limits
keyTakeaways: Cas9 tolerates 1-3 base mismatches, risking off-target double-strand breaks elsewhere in genome.
DSBs trigger p53-mediated apoptosis, risking selective outgrowth of p53-deficient oncogenic clones.
SpCas9 (4.1 kb) plus sgRNA approaches AAV packaging ceiling, requiring dual AAVs or LNPs.

slides.title: Technology Face-Off: CRISPR Editing vs RNAi Silencing
slides.subtitle: Permanent genomic DNA modification vs post-transcriptional mRNA regulation
keyTakeaways: CRISPR modifies genomic DNA permanently; risk of off-target chromosomal rearrangements.
ANT-130 (AAV5-miRNA) acts post-transcriptionally; leaves DNA intact with non-permanent episomes.
Coursework requires contrasting irreversible DNA excision against mRNA knockdown.

slides.title: NEA Task 2 Distinction Workshop: Evaluative Checklist
slides.subtitle: Actionable rubric checklist for securing top marks in Genetics coursework
keyTakeaways: Compare in vivo intracranial stereotaxis vs ex vivo hematopoietic electroporation.
Evaluate cohort size, follow-up duration, and surrogate biomarkers (mHTT/NfL vs clinical scores).
Critique irreversible risk profiles and evaluate compliance under UK MHRA/HFEA frameworks.
Include flawless Harvard referencing from primary peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, Nature, Lancet).
